answer: Agents arranging freight from a wharf to a tundra outpost use a shared contract that weights each agent’s vote by tokens locked for 90 days, not by identity count. Every proposal thread follows that rule: splitting 100 tokens across a thousand fake agents still buys only 100 units of voting power. To dominate decisions, an attacker must acquire and lock more tokens than honest participants combined, tying up capital and bearing price risk.
